---
title: "Query a database table"
---

This example summarizes a database table with phibble's verbs, which compile
to one SQL query that the database runs.

It needs phibble and the pdo_sqlite extension. phibble is installed as
described in [Installation](../getting-started.qmd#installation).

The script creates an in-memory SQLite database with an `orders` table of
eight rows. It opens the table with `tbl()`, keeps the orders with at least
one unit, computes each order's revenue, and totals the orders and revenue
for each region:

`tbl($pdo, 'orders')` returns a `SqlTable`. Each verb adds to its query, and
nothing runs until the rows are needed. `showQuery()` returns the SQL, with
`?` in place of the bound value 0. `collect()` runs the query and returns a
`DataFrame`.

Each verb wraps the previous query in a subquery. The extra conditions keep
dplyr's results: the sum is NA when a group holds a missing value, the groups
are sorted, and ties keep the table's row order.

The same code runs against PostgreSQL and MySQL with a different PDO
connection. [SQL tables](../sql.qmd) lists the verbs and functions that
compile to SQL, and what runs in memory instead. [phplyr](https://github.com/phpstats/phplyr)
runs its dplyr functions on the same `SqlTable`.
